sections.h2: Where is Bacon County, Georgia, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Bacon County sits in southeast Georgia and its county seat is Alma. The county covers 286 square miles, of which 259 are land and 27 are water, according to the Census Bureau figures repeated on Wikipedia.

Georgia voters ratified the amendment creating the county on November 3, 1914. Most of the western half drains to the Satilla River, and the eastern edge drains to the Little Satilla River. Appling, Pierce, Ware, Coffee and Jeff Davis counties border it. Alma is the only incorporated city; Rockingham is a census-designated place, and Coffee and Sessoms are unincorporated communities.

The Census Bureau counts 11,070 residents in its July 2025 estimate, close to the 11,140 counted in 2020. Population per square mile is about 39, so most Bacon County houses sit on rural lots rather than in subdivisions. That matters for sellers, because a rural parcel often carries acreage, a well, a septic system and a long driveway that a buyer will price in.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Bacon County homes?
sections.html:
Bacon County is one of the lower-priced housing markets in the state. The Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $101,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 68.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied.

Only 14 building permits were counted in 2025, so new construction rarely competes with a resale. A resident base that stays put (93.3 percent lived in the same house a year earlier) also means fewer listings at any one time. A seller with a dated or inherited house is mostly competing with other older homes.

sections.h2: Which Bacon County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the same building, the Bacon County Government Building at 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. The tax commissioner bills and collects, and the Board of Tax Assessors sets values and takes homestead applications. The office phone printed on the Bacon County Tax Commissioner site is 912-632-5614, and the stated hours are 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

The Clerk of Superior Court is at Suite 200 of the same address, and that is where you request a copy of a warranty deed. Property records can also be searched on qPublic. If you are untangling a parcel before listing it, a short list of the three counters you may need is:

  • Suite 101: tax bills, payments, lien questions and homestead filings
  • Suite 101: assessment notices, returns and appeals
  • Suite 200: deeds and recorded documents

sections.h2: When are Bacon County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The county site says Bacon County property taxes are generally due by November 15. Bills go out at least 60 days ahead, and the bill itself carries the date that controls, because the county notes it may change.

Payments can be made in two installments, but interest and penalty apply to whatever is unpaid on the due date. If the date lands on a weekend or holiday, you have the next business day at the counter. Mailed checks must be postmarked by the due date, and a drive-up drop box sits at the right side of the front parking lot. Credit cards are accepted, with a 2.75 percent convenience fee and a $2.00 minimum set by the card processor.

  • Interest: the bank prime loan rate plus 3 percent, added each month after the due date
  • Penalty: 5 percent of the tax due, assessed 120 days after the due date and again every 120 days, capped at 20 percent
  • Exception: the penalty does not apply to homesteaded property with a bill under $500
  • Mobile or manufactured homes: due April 1, with a 10 percent penalty if unpaid

sections.h2: What happens if Bacon County taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
After 30 days past the due date, the tax commissioner can record a lien called a FiFa with the Clerk of Superior Court. The county says that lien can stay on a credit record for at least seven years, and that the office does not mail delinquent bills monthly, so you should confirm the balance before you pay.

A lien is recorded against whoever owned the property on January 1 unless the office gets proof of who owes it. If you sold and the taxes were prorated at closing, bring the closing statement to the tax commissioner within 90 days of the due date, and the lien can then be recorded against the new owner. The same page tells sellers to forward any bill that arrives after a sale to the buyer.

For a seller, the practical sequence is simple. Get the payoff balance from Suite 101, ask the title company to pay it from proceeds, and keep a copy of the settlement statement. If the house is behind on several years of tax, ask for a written balance for each year so nothing is missed at the table.

sections.h2: How does a Bacon County appeal work?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the assessment notice to dispute the value. The appeal can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and it starts with a written filing at the Board of Tax Assessors on the state's uniform appeal form.

In that first filing you pick one of three routes: the Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or arbitration. If the assessors change the value, you have 30 days to appeal the new notice. A Board of Equalization decision can be taken to Superior Court. Arbitration requires a certified appraisal and its result is final.

Owners can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 declaring a different value. Real property returns renew automatically each year at the previous value, while personal property returns must be filed every year.

sections.h2: What exemptions and relief can Bacon County owners use?
sections.html:
Homestead exemptions come from the state constitution, and Bacon County adds local exemptions that replace the state amount whenever the local amount is larger. You must own and live in the home on January 1, and the application must be received by April 1 of the first year you claim it. After approval it renews on its own until you move or change ownership.

  • Deferral: owners 62 or older with household income of $15,000 or less may defer tax on the homestead
  • Agricultural property can be assessed at 30 percent instead of 40 percent
  • Conservation use and forest land programs require a covenant of 10 or 15 years
  • Historic and hazardous-site reuse programs also file between January 1 and April 1

Ask the assessor's office at 912-632-5614 for the current local exemption amounts. Do not file a homestead claim on a second property anywhere, since the county notes that doing so is unlawful.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Bacon County house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Start by getting the exact balance and deciding whether it will be paid from the sale. In Bacon County, a rural lot, an inherited house or a mobile home with unpaid tax can all be sold, because the lien is paid at closing like any other charge against title.

Mobile homes carry a separate rule: tax is due April 1 and a location permit must be obtained when you pay. If the home is part of the sale, confirm that year is paid. If the land is enrolled in a conservation or forest program, call the assessor before listing and ask what the covenant requires of a new owner.

A title search will turn up any recorded tax lien, so clear that line before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: What is the assessment rate in Bacon County?
faqs.a: The assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and tax is calculated on that figure after exemptions. The millage rate is set each year by the Board of County Commissioners and the Board of Education.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bacon County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the tax commissioner in Suite 101 of the Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Alma, by mail, in the drop box, or online through the county's payment link. Call 912-632-5614 with questions.

faqs.q: Does the tax commissioner prorate tax between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: The county's own pages say that if taxes were prorated at closing, you should bring the closing statement to the office within 90 days of the due date. The proration itself is handled by your closing paperwork.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund after selling mid-year?
faqs.a: No refund is available for part of a year. Georgia's Department of Revenue says the January 1 owner is responsible for the whole year's tax, even if the property sells on January 2.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Tax Assessors at 912-632-5614 in the same building. They send the assessment notice and take appeals within 45 days of it.
